name: Nuranang (Jang) Falls
tagline: A 100 m waterfall off NH-13 near Jang, 40 km before Tawang
best_time: April to June and September to November, when the flow is strong and the road from Sela is usually clear.

permit.indians: Tourist eILP for Arunachal Pradesh (about Rs 300 to 500; pay what eilp.arunachal.gov.in shows; valid 15 days for the whole state). No extra permit for the falls.
permit.foreigners: Protected Area Permit (PAP) covering Tawang district, arranged through a registered Indian tour operator. Royalty is reported at USD 30–50 per person and the permit at 30 days; confirm with your operator.

ideal_stay: A 45 to 60 minute stop on the Sela–Tawang drive
meta_description: Nuranang (Jang) Falls guide: a 100 m waterfall near Jang, 40 km from Tawang, best season, the short detour from NH-13, permits and travel tips.
quick_answer: Nuranang Falls, also called Jang or Bong Bong Falls, is a 100 m waterfall about 2 km from Jang and roughly 40 km before Tawang on NH-13. The Nuranang Chu flows down from Sela Pass. It is a short detour from the main road. Indians need an eILP, foreigners a PAP. Flow peaks after the monsoon.
intro: After the long descent from Sela, the road reaches Jang, and just beyond the village a side road drops towards a column of white water. Nuranang Chu, fed by the lakes and snow of Sela, pours about 100 m over a cliff in two drops and throws spray across the viewing area even in winter.

A small hydel plant sits near the base and supplies local power. The falls became known outside Arunachal after a song from the 1997 film Koyla was shot here, and drivers on the Tawang road still call it the Koyla falls. The Jang name comes from the village above.

We almost always stop here on the way up to Tawang, when everyone needs to stretch after Sela. Allow 45 minutes: a short walk down, time at the viewpoint, and a tea at one of the stalls by the turn-off.

highlights.name: 100 m drop
highlights.text: One of the taller waterfalls on the Tawang road, falling in two stages into a rocky gorge.

highlights.name: Short detour
highlights.text: The viewpoint is a few hundred metres off NH-13 near Jang, reached by a small road and a short walk.

highlights.name: Snowmelt from Sela
highlights.text: Nuranang Chu rises on the northern slopes of Sela Pass and joins the Tawang river downstream.

highlights.name: Film history
highlights.text: A song from Koyla (1997) was filmed here, among the first Bollywood shoots in Arunachal Pradesh.

things_to_do: Walk down to the lower viewpoint and feel the spray
Photograph the falls in morning light, before cloud comes up the valley
Pair the stop with Jaswantgarh memorial and Sela Pass on the same drive
Have tea and Maggi at the stalls near the turn-off
Look at the small hydel plant near the base that powers the area
Stop at Jang village for a short break before the final 40 km to Tawang
how_to_reach: Nuranang Falls is about 2 km from Jang on NH-13, roughly 40 km before Tawang and on the northern side of Sela. From Dirang it is about 95 km and 3.5 to 4 hours including a Sela stop; from Tezpur about 280 km, which most people split with a night at Dirang or Bomdila. A small road turns off the highway near Jang and leads down to the viewpoint, followed by a short walk. From Tawang it makes a good half-day outing, about 1.5 hours each way. Roads between Sela and Jang can be hit by snow and landslides; check current status before you travel.
where_to_stay: There are basic guesthouses and homestays in Jang village, but almost everyone stays in Tawang, about 40 km and 1.5 hours away, where there is a wider choice of hotels and homestays. If you are coming up from the plains, sleep at Dirang or Bomdila the night before and visit the falls on the way to Tawang. On the way down, the falls are an easy stop before crossing Sela or entering the Sela Tunnel.
tips: The path and viewpoint are wet and slippery; wear shoes with grip
Flow is strongest from June to October, but monsoon cloud can hide the falls
Do not climb on the rocks near the base; the current is strong
In winter the edges can ice over and the side road may be closed; ask locally
Mobile signal is patchy here; the nearest ATMs are in Tawang
Keep the stop to under an hour if you still have Sela ahead of you

faqs.q: How far is Nuranang Falls from Tawang?
faqs.a: Nuranang Falls is about 40 km from Tawang town, near Jang village on NH-13. The drive takes around 1.5 hours each way. Most travellers stop on their way up from Dirang and Sela Pass rather than making a separate trip, since the falls lie directly on the main Tawang road.

faqs.q: What is the height of Nuranang Falls?
faqs.a: Nuranang Falls drops about 100 m in two stages. It is fed by the Nuranang Chu, which rises on the northern side of Sela Pass and later joins the Tawang river. A small hydel plant near the base generates electricity for local use.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit Nuranang Falls?
faqs.a: No separate permit is needed for the falls. Indian citizens need the Arunachal Pradesh tourist eILP (about Rs 300 to 500 per person, as shown on the portal), and foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit. Both are checked at the entry gate at Bhalukpong and at posts along the road.

Yes. The falls lie on the main road to Tawang, which is open to foreign nationals holding a Protected Area Permit arranged by a registered Indian tour operator. Unlike Bum La, there are no extra restrictions here. Check current PAP rules with your operator before booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see Nuranang Falls?
faqs.a: Water flow is strongest from June to October, but September to November gives the best mix of full falls and clear skies. April to June is also good. In winter the flow drops and edges can freeze, and snow at Sela can hold up the road. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Why is Nuranang also called Jang Falls?
faqs.a: The falls are named after the Nuranang river, and Jang is the nearest village, about 2 km away, so drivers often call it Jang Falls. It is also known locally as Bong Bong Falls, and some visitors call it the Koyla falls because a song from that 1997 film was shot here.

faqs.q: Is Nuranang Falls safe for children and seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. The walk from the parking area to the viewpoint is short, but the steps and rocks are wet from spray. Hold children's hands, keep away from the edge and the base of the falls, and let seniors take the path slowly. The altitude is lower than Sela, so breathing is easier.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network or an ATM near Nuranang Falls?
faqs.a: Mobile signal is patchy around Jang and the falls; you may get BSNL or Airtel briefly. There are no ATMs at the falls or in Jang, so draw cash in Dirang or Tawang. Small tea stalls near the turn-off accept cash and sometimes UPI when there is signal.

faqs.q: How long do I need at Nuranang Falls?
faqs.a: Around 45 minutes to an hour is enough for the walk down, time at the viewpoint and a tea at the stalls. If you are driving from Dirang to Tawang the same day, keep it short so you reach Tawang before dark, especially in winter when the light goes by 5 pm.
